title: bison Security Beyond the Single-Key Model
summary: The bison construction is claimed to provide n-bit security only in the single-key model; security in the related-key, chosen-key, and known-key models remains unresolved.

formal_statement.body: The \textsf{bison} construction is claimed to provide $n$-bit security in the single-key model, but no security is claimed in the related-key, chosen-key, or known-key models. Determine whether \textsf{bison} is secure in each of these three models by either establishing an appropriate security result or exhibiting an attack that refutes security.

scope.domain: Security analysis of the bison symmetric block-cipher construction across multiple key models.
parameters: n: the claimed security level in bits
scope.unresolved_remainder: Establish an appropriate security result for bison, or exhibit an attack that refutes its security, in each of the related-key, chosen-key, and known-key models.

citations.label: bison Instantiating the Whitened Swap-Or-Not Construction

progress.summary: The source states a single-key n-bit security claim and explicitly disclaims security claims in the related-key, chosen-key, and known-key models. It presents security in those three models as unresolved.
citation_labels: Anne Canteaut et al., bison Instantiating the Whitened Swap-Or-Not Construction
